extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, patent practitioners, and stakeholders filing or defending Chinese patents (especially utility models)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the CNIPA's amended Patent Examination Guidelines (effective Jan 20, 2024), focusing on the introduction of preliminary inventiveness examination for utility models and how inventiveness/novelty will be judged for utility models versus invention patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination of utility models for obvious lack of novelty and inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: During the preliminary examination, the examiner will examine whether the utility model patent application obviously lacks novelty and inventiveness. The examiner can examine whether the utility model patent application obviously lacks novelty based on the information he obtains about the prior art or conflicting applications. The examiner can examine whether a utility model patent application obviously lacks inventive step based on the information he or she has obtained about the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Part I, Chapter 2, Section 11 (page 70). For novelty, refer to Chapter 3 of Part II and Chapter 6, Section 3 of Part IV of the Guidelines. For inventive step, refer to Section 4 of Chapter 6 of Part IV. This introduces substantive scrutiny at preliminary stage for utility models (which historically lacked substantive examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of all technical features in inventiveness review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the examination of the inventiveness of a utility model patent, all technical features of the technical solution, including material features and method features, should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: Section 4 of Chapter 6 of Part IV (page 453) concerning inventiveness review in invalidation proceedings. Examiner should not ignore material or method features when assessing inventiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower inventiveness standard for utility models versus invention patents
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Article 22(3) of the Patent Law and the Guidelines, the standard of creativity (inventiveness) for utility model patents should be lower than that for invention patents: the concept of creativity requires 'outstanding substantive features and significant progress compared with the existing technology', but the threshold for utility models is lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance explains that both invention and utility model require outstanding substantive features and significant progress vs. existing technology, but in practice the inventiveness judgment standard differs primarily in how 'technical inspiration' from prior art is assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of existing technology considered in inventiveness assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: For invention patents, assess not only the technical field of the invention but also similar or related technical fields and technical problems that could prompt skilled persons to search other fields. For utility model patents, the general focus is on the technical field to which the utility model belongs; similar or related fields may be considered only if prior art gives clear inspiration prompting such a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction affects the scope of prior art and analogous fields considered when determining whether a skilled person would be prompted to combine or adapt prior art to arrive at the claimed solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity and combination of prior art used to evaluate inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: For invention patents, one, two or more prior art documents can be cited to evaluate inventiveness. For utility model patents, one or two prior art documents can generally be cited to evaluate inventiveness. For utility models formed by a 'simple superposition' of existing technologies, multiple prior art documents may be cited depending on the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance signals that utility models are typically evaluated against fewer prior art references and that combining many references to defeat inventiveness is less readily applied to utility models unless the claimed utility model is an obvious simple combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior art and conflicting applications in preliminary novelty examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may examine whether a utility model application obviously lacks novelty based on the information they obtain about prior art or conflicting applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits examiners at the preliminary stage to rely on available prior art and any conflicting pending/granted applications to make a preliminary novelty determination; referral to the Guidelines' chapters on novelty for detailed criteria.
